research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
regression to the mean in absence selection
methodological_questions: How should reorganization magnitude relative to L be defined and fixed before analysis?
Does reorganization magnitude predict the subsequent change in PPP, net of team quality and baseline efficiency?
What minimum detectable effect does the spell count (n=148) support?
Do play-type-derived measures leak the outcome, and can they be made lookahead-free?
Does selecting spells by extreme absence produce regression-to-the-mean artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: Absence validation. Within [APPA-006]/[APPA-007]/[PAP-023], real absences moved the association structure (V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]). The magnitude prediction from the leave-one-out simulation (V2a rho +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667]; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115) failed. Recorded limitation: LIM:small_sample.

Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence: unmatched 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97; usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96. Versus terminal: +0.0777, p=0.0261, n=25. Recorded risks: MECHANICAL_FLOOR, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. This is a displacement measure, not a PPP outcome.

Play-type decaying cross-possession memory. Flat lifts (+0.015 to +0.021) did not decay across lags; within-team baseline collapsed the effect (DRIVE lag-1 +0.015 to -0.002). Recorded as a team-quality confound; verdict failed_gate.

BEST-vs-continue gap after a slump was +0.248 (SE 0.009), but the same gap appeared without a slump (+0.239) and under a fixed CUT-heavy ranking (+0.238). Recorded as a construction artifact with BASE_RATE risk.

Within-game defensive adaptation to repeated play types was -0.0019 PPP per exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Effects above about 0.02 were ruled out after 5 exposures. Only PULL_UP survived Holm correction (B -0.0243, holm p=0.0004). Recorded limits: insufficient exposure, label/classification error, low measurement reliability.

Similarity of replacement play-type profiles did not separate absorption from cascade when a player sat (mean sim ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed). Recorded failure type B_powered_null, with observed_sample_and_power NOT_RECORDED.

Post-hoc matched-pair test of abandon-vs-continue suppressed play types on overall offense: group A excess +0.076 [+0.068, +0.084] (n=3421); group B +0.014 [-0.019, +0.046] (n=255, 242 games); gap -0.062. Recorded as a reconstructed post-hoc cohort with PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks.

Pre-game play-type PPP ranking from training data correlated with held-out efficiency ranking (median rho +0.539; 88.4% rho>0), with a caveat that top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types. Relevant only as a reminder that play-type baselines carry league-level structure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of structural change under absence from a simulation (V2a/V2b).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as not significant (p=0.077 and p=0.115) with wide CIs spanning zero; limitation LIM:small_sample. Structure-change detection (V1) worked, but magnitude prediction did not.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Persistent cross-possession play-type memory as an explanation of PPP change.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a team-quality confound; flat lifts collapsed under a within-team baseline.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Slump-conditioned gap as evidence of costly failure to abandon a play.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a construction artifact: the gap was identical without a slump event.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Replacement-profile similarity as a discriminator of absorption versus cascade.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null, with the sign wrong; no sample/power recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matched-pair abandon-vs-continue comparison on overall offense.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: the post-hoc group B CI includes zero and the cohort is not validated.

evidence_establishes: Absences do move the team's association structure (FAM:SF20, V1 confirmed; FAM:SF-APPS-088 shows large identity displacement for connector absence). A reorganization index can therefore detect real change.

Several earlier attempts to link play-type dynamics to PPP-level outcomes ended as artifacts, null, or untestable (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-063, FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-APPS-025). Confounding by team quality and label error are recorded hazards for this kind of outcome.
Power in earlier studies was often small or not recorded, so the historical record gives no reliable estimate of an effect size for reorganization versus PPP change.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests reorganization magnitude relative to baseline L against change in PPP. The question is not answered by prior work, and the retrieved records do not define L.
No record gives an effect size or variance for the reorganization-PPP association, so the expected power for n=148 spells is unknown from history.
Whether the 986 units (the recorded unit count) relate to the 148 spells is not stated in any record. Which unit the test uses is unresolved.
Whether the 2025-26 partial files would contaminate the analysis is not addressed in any record.
own_inferences: A two-sided test on n=148 spells at alpha 0.05 and 80% power has a minimum detectable correlation of about 0.23 (inference from the standard Fisher-z approximation). Smaller true associations would be missed, so a null would be weakly informative.
The question is ill-posed until the baseline L and the PPP-change window are fixed. Without that, the estimand is not identified.

Given that the magnitude prediction failed at small n (FAM:SF20) and that PPP-level play-type claims have repeatedly collapsed to artifacts, a clean positive result seems unlikely. The most probable outcome is an underpowered or confounded null.
uncertainties: The meaning of 'n=986' and 'mde rho' in the unit field is not defined; the recorded MDE value is absent.
The definition of L (a prior period, a lineup baseline, or a season average) is not given.
The definition of 'change in PPP' (window length, pre- versus post-absence, team versus player level) is not given.
No retrieved record reports a validation status (all show no_validation_recorded or NOT_RECORDED), so reproducibility is unknown.
Only 10 of the tool-returnable families were examined; additional families might bear on this question but were not retrieved.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that reorganization can be measured (FAM:SF20 V1; FAM:SF-APPS-088) but that several outcome-level play-type claims failed through confounding, label error, or low power (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-CHT-063, FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF38). That moved the decision from an open-ended test to a conditional proceed: only with a fixed baseline L, a pre-specified outcome window, team-quality controls, placebo windows, and an explicit MDE statement.

blocking_constraints.text: 148 spells give an MDE near rho 0.23; smaller true effects will not be detected, and the 986-unit count is not reconciled with the spell count.
L and the PPP-change window are undefined, so the estimand is not identified until they are fixed.
Team quality, usage and rotation changes covary with absences and PPP; prior records show team-quality confounds collapsing play-type effects.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work establishes that absences move association structure (FAM:SF20 V1) and that connector absence displaces team identity (FAM:SF-APPS-088). It does not test reorganization relative to baseline L against change in PPP. Related PPP-level play-type studies were artifacts, null, or untestable, with confounding and power the recurring problems.

risks.text: n=148 spells: MDE about rho 0.23; the earlier magnitude prediction failed at small n (FAM:SF20).
Spells with few possessions in the pre or post window give noisy PPP.
Reorganization is a derived index with no reliability estimate in the records; team-trait split-half reliability was low in FAM:SF38.
Selecting spells by large absence or large reorganization guarantees regression toward the mean in PPP change.
Play-type labels built from the same play-by-play as PPP can embed the outcome.
Windows that include post-absence possessions when defining the reorganization index leak the outcome.
Play-type classification error (recorded as a limit in FAM:SF38 and FAM:SF-CHT-052) can bias the reorganization measure.
Team quality, opponent strength, and minutes changes confound the association (FAM:SF-CHT-029).
Post-hoc cohorts (FAM:SF-APPS-025) make results depend on construction choices.
Many reorganization definitions and windows would inflate false positives.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 files mixes league and roster regimes.
Absence frequency and PPP base rates vary by team and season.

design.estimand: Partial association (Spearman, net of team and baseline controls) between the pre-registered reorganization index relative to baseline L and the change in team PPP from the pre-absence window to the post-absence window, per absence spell.
design.unit: Absence spell (team x player absence episode), with spells clustered by team and season.
design.sample: 148 spells from complete regular-season files (2022-23 to 2024-25, plus 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13). Exclude partial 2025-26 files and playoffs. Reconcile the 986-unit count with the spell count before analysis.
design.power: At alpha 0.05 two-sided and 80% power, n=148 gives MDE |rho| about 0.23 (inference). Report the MDE and a sensitivity curve; do not claim a null below that threshold.
design.controls: Team fixed effects or pre-absence team PPP; opponent strength; minutes and usage shift; pace; spell length. Define L before outcome data are seen, using only pre-absence possessions. Compute the reorganization index from features excluding the outcome window to avoid lookahead. Use play-type labels independent of the PPP outcome where possible.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo windows shifted before the absence should show no association. (b) Same index computed in games without absence should be null. (c) Negative-control outcome (for example, defensive rating change) should not track the index.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary test. Secondary definitions of L and the window are reported as sensitivity analyses with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Support only if the primary partial rho's cluster-bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0 in the pre-registered direction, the placebo and negative-control tests are null, and the result survives the alternative L definition. Otherwise report as uncertain or rejected at the MDE, and flag an artifact if placebo windows reproduce the effect.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoff seasons; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Exclude partial 2025-26 regular-season and playoff files; the playoff snapshot is not complete as of 2026-11-01, so exclude it.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: how to measure the magnitude of offensive reorganization relative to a baseline lineup or period L
whether reorganization predicts subsequent change in points per possession
sample size and minimum detectable effect for spell-level analyses
regression to the mean and selection of spells with extreme absences
outcome-derived labels and lookahead leakage in play-type measures
args.query: player absence offensive reorganization relative to baseline L predicts change in points per possession, spells, play-type possession records, minimum detectable effect rho

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
